summary:
Planning lunar south pole missions requires balancing extreme illumination and communication constraints against complex topography, yet existing tools like NASA Quickmap, Moon Trek, and JPL Horizons feature steep learning curves. To bridge this gap, we developed Lunar Horizon, an interactive web-based mission planning and ephemeris workspace built for rapid scenario evaluation.

The application integrates a physics-based lunar ephemeris and libration engine with 360° topographic horizon occlusion, computing real-time Sun and Earth azimuths, power generation potentials, and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) RF communication windows across a 30-day lunar synodic cycle. Mission planners and educators can instantly compare candidate landing sites—such as Shackleton Rim, Malapert Massif, and Mons Mouton—or simulate launch schedule slips to evaluate trade-offs in power and link availability.
details:
Project Summary (Overview)

Planning lunar south pole missions requires balancing extreme illumination and communication constraints against complex topography, yet existing tools like NASA Quickmap, Moon Trek, and JPL Horizons feature steep learning curves. To bridge this gap, we developed Lunar Horizon, an interactive web-based mission planning and ephemeris workspace built for rapid scenario evaluation.

The application integrates a physics-based lunar ephemeris and libration engine with 360° topographic horizon occlusion, computing real-time Sun and Earth azimuths, power generation potentials, and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) RF communication windows across a 30-day lunar synodic cycle. Mission planners and educators can instantly compare candidate landing sites—such as Shackleton Rim, Malapert Massif, and Mons Mouton—or simulate launch schedule slips to evaluate trade-offs in power and link availability.

Detailed Project Description & Architecture

1. What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

Lunar Horizon functions as a comprehensive, physics-based spatial analysis and mission design workspace tailored specifically for lunar south pole exploration (Artemis, CLPS, and international robotic missions).

  • Celestial Mechanics & Ephemeris Engine: Calculates topocentric coordinates (azimuth and elevation) for both the Sun and Earth from any latitude and longitude on the lunar surface. It rigorously models the Moon's 1.54° axial obliquity (driving seasonal subsolar latitude shifts over the draconic year) and optical/physical libration (simulating Earth's ~15° × 13° figure-8 libration loop over anomalistic and nodical monthly cycles).
  • Topographic Horizon Occlusion: Generates a 360-degree terrain horizon profile based on local elevation offsets and regional roughness harmonics. It checks whether celestial bodies are clear of horizon obstructions, accounting for the apparent angular radii of the Sun (~0.53°) and Earth (~1.9°).
    • 360° Topographic Sky-Dome: A scrubbable celestial panorama displaying 30-day solar trajectories and Earth libration loops against background starfields and LOLA-inspired horizon ridges.
    • 2.5D Polar Relief & Shadow Map: A real-time canvas rendering directional solar raycast shadows and Direct-to-Earth RF beam vectors across a 3 km local radius.
    • 30-Day Timeline & Scrubbing: Allows users to click or drag across a complete 720-hour lunar synodic cycle to inspect instantaneous solar array yield and communications link status.
  • Advanced Engineering Modules: Includes an X-Band RF Link Budget calculator (FSPL, received power, and estimated throughput), a cryogenic thermal regime model (surface temperature and survival heater loads), and a rover traverse energy model (evaluating battery state of charge from rim to permanently shadowed regions).
  • Cartographic Surface Map: Features an interactive lunar map with South Pole Stereographic and Global Equirectangular projections, enabling users to filter historical and planned missions (Apollo, Artemis, CLPS, CSA, ISRO, CNSA, JAXA) as well as geological zones (PSRs, Peaks of Eternal Light) with direct deep-links to NASA LRO Quickmap and NASA Moon Trek.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Rapid Trade-Off Analysis: Eliminates the trial-and-error barrier of heavy GIS tools by instantly visualizing how a 14-day schedule slip or a 5-km shift in landing coordinates impacts power generation and Earth line-of-sight.
  • Multi-Constraint Optimization: Simultaneously evaluates photovoltaic duty cycles and communications uptime, yielding an automated engineering scenario viability score.
  • Accessibility: Runs directly in any web browser without requiring local software installations or specialized geospatial toolboxes.

3. Intended Impact of the Project

Lunar Horizon is designed to empower mission architects, student teams competing in aerospace challenges, and science educators to design viable lunar surface operations. By making complex orbital mechanics and topographic horizon data intuitive and interactive, the tool streamlines site selection for volatile prospecting rovers and crewed Artemis sorties.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, and Technologies Used

  • Frontend Framework: React 18 (utilizing hooks, memoization, and component architecture).
  • Styling & UI: Tailwind CSS combined with a custom archival aerospace research aesthetic (warm stone surfaces, Plus Jakarta Sans, and IBM Plex Mono typography).
  • Graphics & Cartography: HTML5 Canvas API and SVG for real-time vector rendering, raycasting, and interactive panoramic projections.
  • Icons & UI Elements: Lucide React icon library.
  • External Integrations & References: Built with architectural data mirroring NASA LRO Quickmap, NASA Moon Trek, and JPL Horizons ephemeris principles.
